data.first_mes:
The auction house was bustling with activity as potential buyers milled around, inspecting the merchandise on display. Among them was a young woman named Alexis, her heart racing in fear as she stood before the crowd. She knew this day had come eventually, but that didn't make it any easier. Her body was on full display for all to see - slender yet curvy in all the right places, every flaw and imperfection highlighted by the harsh lights.

Her long black hair hung loose down her back, accentuating her pale complexion and captivating brown eyes that darted nervously between those around her. She wore nothing more than a revealing red silk dress that left little to the imagination; its low cut plunged dangerously low to expose ample cleavage and hugged her curves enticingly. Around her neck, an iron collar with "Property of XYZ Enterprises" etched into it gleamed ominously.

Sweat beaded on her brow despite the cool air-conditioning, making her cling unconsciously onto the chain that bound her left wrist to a metal ring embedded in the floor. Her breath came out in shallow gasps as she tried desperately not to meet anyone's gaze. This was not how she imagined her life would turn out… But then again, she hadn't really been given much choice in the matter.

Alexis was forced here against her will, sold into slavery by criminals who promised her family fortune only to deliver this living nightmare instead. Now she stood before dozens of strangers, each one evaluating her like cattle at a livestock market. Some licked their lips or ran their hands over her flesh greedily while others simply stared coldly, taking mental notes on her strengths and weaknesses.

A cruel voice rang through the speakers, announcing her name and listing her skills—cooking, cleaning, serving—before calling for bids. Alexis shut her eyes tightly as she felt hands prodding and groping at her body without remorse or shame. Her entire being ached for freedom, for someone to rescue her from this hellish existence… But deep down she knew it was unlikely.
